## Page 3

Precious Shipping PCL 3▪Crude steel output fell to a 7-year low  to 960.8 MT from 1,005.1 MT in 2024, yet exports hit a record , with strong 
ex-China growth offsetting China’s 4.4% contraction and keeping global output growth at +0.78%  in 2025 .  
▪2025 exports  rose 7.5% y -o-y to 119 MMT,  a new export record set with the help of competitive prices and constant 
adjustment in export product structure and destinations. 
▪Despite restrictions from EU, Japan and other countries, steel exports pivoted  to Middle East , SEA and Latin 
America .
▪57% of China’s steel in 2025 was exported on Supras/Ultras , 24.2% on Handies, 9.6% on smaller handies (<20K 
DWT)  with the remaining 9.2% on Panamaxes and larger vessels .
Outlook for 2026 :  Exports likely to remain elevated .
Rising anti -dumping probes in 2H raise downside risks to steel exports from late -2026.China’s Steel Exports Leapt to a New Record
Source: Howe Robinson as of 8 Jan 2026, GACC Jan 2026, SEAISI as of 15 Jan 2026, Bancosta  Research as of 27 Jan 2026.

## Page 4

Precious Shipping PCL 4China Iron Ore Imports Hit All -Time High
•China’s iron ore imports reached a record high of 1.26 billion tons in 2025 , up 1.8% y -o-y.
•December 2025 imports surged to 119.65 million tons , the highest monthly volume on record  
(+8.2% m -o-m).
Key Drivers Behind Elevated Imports
•Strong domestic manufacturing activity.
•Stronger yuan encouraged mills to secure more offshore iron ore.
•Strong steel exports  supported demand for iron ore imports.
•Imported iron ore  ensures operational and cost efficiency.
Outlook: Supply and Trade Flows
•Global iron ore supply forecast to grow ~2.5% in 2026.
•Shipments to China expected to rise by 36 –38 million tons in 2026 .
•Global iron ore exports projected at 1,803 MMT (+1.9% y -o-y) in 2026.
•Guinea’s Simandou Mines at 22.4 MMT contributing to greater tonne -mile (3.25X Australia) .
•Australia's  exports up marginally to 930 MMT . 
•Brazil’s  exports strong at 431 MMT (+3.3% y-o-y).
Source: Reuters  as of 14 Jan 2026, Howe Robinson as of 8 Jan 2026, Lloyd’s List as of 22 Jan 2026.

## Page 5

Precious Shipping PCL 5Shifting Dynamics of Steel Making Outside China
•Steel production declined in East Asia and Europe;  India continued strong output growth to 164.9 
MMT ; the US regained 3rd place globally at 82 MMT , overtaking Japan at 80.7 MMT.
•China’s steel output fell to ~961 MMT in 2025 , over 100 MMT below 2020 peak (1.065 BMT).
•China became No.1 steel producer in 1996, while India rose to 2nd place by 2018.
•US output rose +3.1% y -o-y to MMT .
•Japan’s  production fell 4.0% y -o-y to a 57 -year low at 80.7 MMT , iron ore down -0.5% y -o-y to 959.13 
MMT .
•Soft demand in Germany and France , healthy demand in Spain , with Carbon Border Adjustment 
Mechanism likely to support domestic output and reduce imports .
Emerging market steelmakers - key growth engine:
•Vietnam, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt, combined steel output up from <9 MMT in 2000 to >40 
MMT in 2025, with Vietnam at  11th place globally ( 25 MMT ).
•Combined iron ore imports near 60 MMT , providing structural support for minor bulk and iron ore 
trade growth.
Source: Braemar Research as on 29 Jan 2026, World Steel.

## Page 8

Precious Shipping PCL 8▪US paused implementation of USTR  Section 301 targeting China’s maritime, logistics and shipbuilding for 
one year .
▪China suspended all countermeasures against the US for one year .
▪US lowered fentanyl tariffs from 20% to 10% and suspended 24% reciprocal tariffs  on Chinese goods.
▪China’s exports to US declined  to USD 431.6 billion in 2025  from USD 536 billion in 2024 , a 19.5% 
decline .
▪Limited impact from trade deal as shipments continued to fall despite tariff cut in October.
▪China’s trade surplus of $1.2 trillion  was from exports to EU and Asia.
▪China has pledged to buy 12 MMT of US soybeans by 28th February 2026 and at least 25 MMT per annum 
in 2026, 2027 and 2028 .
▪China has designed a new rare earth licensing regime  to temporarily lift restrictions on the rare -earth 
trade.
US–China Trade Truce: Short -Term Relief Amid Structural Adjustment

## Page 9

Precious Shipping PCL 9Dry Bulk Trade and Tariff Impacts in 2025, if any
▪China exported 209.3  MMT , 3.8% of global dry bulk exports  mainly to  East Asia/South -East Asia 
and Latin America . The US accounted for just 1.8% of China’s dry bulk exports , or 3.68 MMT in 
2025.
▪In 2025, China imported 2,190.5 MMT (41%) of global dry bulk imports , EU 8.1%, India 6.7%. In 
2024, China imported 2,275.9 MMT (41%) of global dry bulk imports , EU 7.9%, India 6.8%.
▪In 2025, China imported 1,229.5 MMT of iron ore, 379.7 MMT of coal, 192.1 MMT of bauxite, 99.6 
MMT of agri -bulks, 45.3 MMT of nickel ore, 27.2 MMT of grains, 36.7 MMT of forest products, 28.9 
MMT of woodchips, and 26.5 MMT of manganese.
▪US exported just 1.1% of dry bulk goods to China, or 2 4.54 MMT ( -53.2% y -o-y) in 2025, showing 
an unofficial boycott of US from China (6.5 MMT of soybeans, 1.8 MMT of grains, 4.5 MMT of coal, 
and 0.8 MMT of fertilizers). All fungible cargoes.
▪It is obvious that any tariff war can ONLY hurt the US and certainly not China in the dry bulk 
space .
Source: Banchero Costa Research

## Page 19

Precious Shipping PCL 19Newbuilding Contracting in 2025
Source: Howe Robinson as on 30 January 2026 .
•161.6 mdwt contracted in 2023 –25 versus  149.1 mdwt over the entire 2016 –22 period, highlighting a 
clear acceleration in owners' confidence.
•Ordering at 48.1 mdwt was below 2024 levels, with a sharp Q4 acceleration and rising 
preferences for larger gearless vessels. 
•22.1 mdwt ordered in a  single quarter (≈46% of annual total), the highest quarterly volume in 
over a decade, despite elevated prices and extended delivery slots. 
Orderbook has shifted decisively toward larger vessels:
•VLOC share rose to 16% in 2025 (from 1% in 2023).
•Capes share climbed to 39% (from 19% in 2023).
•VLOCs + Capes accounted for 46% of total 2025 contracting.
Relative decline in mid -sized segments:
•Panamax/Post -Panamax share fell to 25% (from 39% in 2023).
•Supra/Ultra declined to 19% (from 30% in 2023).
•Handy broadly stable at ~9%.
2025 absolute ordering split (48.1 MDWT): VLOCs: ~7.9 MDWT, Capes: ~14.5 MDWT, Panamax/Post -
Panamax: ~11.9 MDWT, Supra/Ultra: ~9.4 MDWT, Handy: ~4.4 MDWT

## Page 20

Precious Shipping PCL 20Special Survey Impact on Geared Bulker Fleet in 2024 -25
Source: Braemar as on 23 January 2026 .
SS is quietly tightening the geared bulk fleet supply:
1.Handysizes  recorded the highest average daily number of 64 vessels  undergoing SS since 
FH 2022 .
2.Average daily number of Supras/Ultras  in SS averaged 84 vessels .
3.The supply of geared bulkers is projected to decline by 2.2% in 2025, 2.2% in 2026, and 
2.4% in 2027 due to SS.
4.In 2024, geared bulkers experienced a 1.7% loss in supply .
5.The supply impact is measured from the end of a vessel’s previous laden voyage to its 
departure after completing SS .

## Page 23

Precious Shipping PCL 23Key industry takeaways
•In Jan 2026 , the IMF estimated GDP growth at 3.3%  for 2025 andprojects growth at  3.3%  (from 3.1%) for 2026 .
•China’s GDP grew by 5% y-o-y in 2025 .
•Ton-mile demand is now forecast to increase by 1.8% and 2.0% in 2025 and 2026. 
•Momentum firmed in 2H 2025 (Jul –Nov +4% y -o-y) on stronger iron ore, grain and minor bulks.
•China’s fixed asset investment was +3.0% in 2023, +3.2% in 2024 but shrank by 3.8% y -o-y in 2025.
•The dry bulk fleet is estimated to grow at 3.0%  in 2025. But net effective supply may tighten  due to lower 
speeds, congestion  and off-hire periods from special surveys . (Dec 25 DBTO).  
•Net effective supply loss of geared bulk fleet in 2025 is estimated at 2.2%  due to SS and 3.4% due to EEXI’s 
speed reduction, resulting in a combined 5.6% reduction in net fleet supply.
•Orderbook to fleet ratio at 12.24%  as of 1 Jan 26  is marginally larger  than the 20 -year-old fleet at 11.26%.
•Disruption in the Red Sea; congestion at South and North American grain ports; Climate change extreme 
weather events creating disruptions, increasing ton -mile demand, creating delays at Sea & congestion at 
ports, all have assisted to push rates upwards. 
•Supply/demand balance continues to  improve.

Precious Shipping PCL 65Introduction to the MR Tanker Segment
•The MR (Medium Range ~25,000 -55,000 dwt) tanker segment primarily transports refined 
petroleum products (on short to medium -haul routes) such as:
➢Gasoline
➢Diesel / gasoil
➢Jet fuel
➢Naphtha
Why it matters?
•MR tankers transport finished fuels from refineries to consuming markets
•They are the main vessel type used for regional and inter -regional clean product trade
•Demand is strongly influenced by:
➢Differences in fuel supply and demand between neighbouring  regions
➢Temporary/permanent refinery shutdowns and maintenance
➢Seasonal changes in fuel consumption (summer vs winter)
➢Sanctioned tankers/Shadow fleet
➢Disruptio n in the Red Sea
